subject: Patchworks Labs: integration delay — request for trial extension and credits
messages:
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -0700
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@patchworkslabs.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Dana Rivera <dana.rivera@patchworkslabs.com>
Subject: Integration blocker: SDK mismatch causing build pause — trial extension + credits?

Hey Logan,

Quick update from our engineering team: after upgrading to your latest client (v2.4.0) we ran into a runtime mismatch when initializing the streaming socket. The Node SDK we vendor against (internal wrapper) expects the older header format, and our engineering lead estimates this will take two dev days to shore up and validate. That pushes our demo window out and stalls the evaluation.

Can Redwood do two things to keep momentum?
- Grant a two-week extension to our sandbox/trial so we can finish the integration after the patch lands.
- Add an extra 150k tokens of sandbox credit (or equivalent) so we can complete the end-to-end load checks without hitting quota.

I've attached a short log excerpt and the error trace (integration-log-snippet.txt, patchworks-stacktrace.png) to help diagnose. We love the performance numbers so far; this is just a timing issue.

If we can get the extension/credits approved this week we can still make the exec demo on Oct 2. Appreciate any help you can provide.

Best,
Ethan

Ethan — thanks for the context and the logs. Sorry to hear you hit this at the last minute.

On Tue, Sep 14, 2026 at 9:02 AM Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@patchworkslabs.com> wrote:
> Quick update from our engineering team: after upgrading to your latest client (v2.4.0) we ran into a runtime mismatch when initializing the streaming socket...

I'm looping in our SRE/solutions engineer Dylan Brooks (dylan_brooks@redwood.com) to verify the trace and propose the minimal workaround, and Kimberly Park on CS to triage the commercial side.

High level: we typically approve short trial extensions for integration blockers, and can issue sandbox credits for load testing if the technical issue is confirmed. To move quickly, can you confirm:
1) Exact SDK version you upgraded from
2) Whether you can run an isolated repro with a small trace (so we can reproduce locally)
3) Your preferred extension length (we'll propose 10–14 days as a starting point)

I can fast-track credit approval once Dylan confirms it's an integration problem and Kimberly signs off on the concession.

— Logan

Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 14:05:00 -0700
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Subject: Re: Integration blocker: SDK mismatch causing build pause — quick technical read

Logan — I pulled the attachments and reproduced the startup failure in a local sandbox. Short summary:
- The client v2.4.0 changed the initial handshake header (X-RW-Stream -> X-RW-Stream-Id) which our server accepts, but the Patchworks wrapper expects the old header and rejects the socket.
- Patchworks can either update their wrapper (preferred) or we can temporarily accept the old header in a compatibility mode for their account.

Impact: a compatibility toggle + a small restart on our side will let their current binary run; no model change required. Time estimate: ~3 hours ops work + toggling back after demo.

Commercial ask: given the delay, I recommend we offer a 14-day trial extension + 150k sandbox tokens so the customer can finish integration and run load tests. That matches other recent concessions for engineering blockers.

If you want to limit exposure we can split the credit (100k now, 50k contingent on demo completion) — happy to draft the approval note.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
SRE / Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 16:10:00 -0700
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Integration blocker: commercial signoff guidance

Thanks for the run-down. A couple of commercial guardrails:
- For sandbox credits tied to technical blockers we prefer a conservative default: 100k tokens + a 10-day extension.
- If engineering can confirm reproducibility and provide a short plan to finish (commit + smoke test), we can stretch to 14 days and add the extra 25k as a discretionary top-up (total 125k).
- Need deal id confirmed before authorizing any tokens (please attach/confirm HubSpot record).

Logan — if you can confirm the HubSpot company id and commit to the follow-up plan we can sign the form and I will route for approval. If Patchworks needs the full 150k immediately we should ask for a brief acceptance email acknowledging the tokens are a one-time support concession tied to this integration issue.

Kimberly Park

Ethan — good news. We reviewed this internally and can support the integration effort with a short concession to keep your demo on track.

Summary of what Redwood will provide:
- 14 calendar day extension of your sandbox/trial starting today (new end date: 2026-09-28).
- 125,000 sandbox tokens applied to your account (Patchworks Labs).

Conditions:
- The tokens/extension are a one-time, goodwill concession tied to the integration blocker noted in your log.
- We ask Patchworks to confirm the HubSpot company record and reply to this thread with a short acceptance line (e.g., "Patchworks accepts the 14-day extension and 125k sandbox tokens") so we have an audit trail.
- Please use the attached trial-credit-approval-form.pdf to acknowledge the concession; sign electronically via DocuSign if easier: https://www.docusign.com/ENVELOPE/12345-abcde.

We also created a temporary compatibility toggle on your account to accept the older handshake header so you can validate immediately. Dylan will handle the toggle and can coordinate a quick hand-off call if you want.

Onward — looking forward to the demo.
